note: Literature supports dominant-negative missense variants causing axonal lysosome accumulation and more severe structural brain anomalies compared to loss-of-function alleles.

evidence.text: Brain anomalies like perisylvian polymicrogyria and atrophy were consistent among patients with recurrent de novo missense variants, and modeled missense alterations in C. elegans caused elevated axonal lysosome density and locomotion defects.

source.title: De novo variants in MAPK8IP3 cause intellectual disability with variable brain anomalies
source.quote: Brain anomalies such as perisylvian polymicrogyria, cerebral or cerebellar atrophy, and hypoplasia of the corpus callosum were consistent among individuals harboring recurrent de novo missense variants... Using the CRISPR-Cas9 system to target six conserved amino acid positions in Caenorhabditis elegans, we found that two of the six investigated human alterations led to a significantly elevated density of axonal lysosomes, and five variants were associated with adverse locomotion.

numbers.metric: missense variants tested in C. elegans showing elevated axonal lysosome density

evidence.text: Clinical evaluation revealed that missense variants are associated with significantly more severe neurological phenotypes than loss-of-function alleles, supporting a potential dominant-negative mechanism.

source.title: Comprehensive Clinical Characteristics, Longitudinal Adaptive Functioning, and Electroencephalogram Activity in MAPK8IP3‐Related Neurodevelopmental Disorder
